items.title: Split augmented simplicial schemes and matching objects
items.axiom_use: No selection is made in the definition; the axiom dependency is inherited from the cited finite-limit and coproduct constructions of schemes.
items.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and work in the category of $S$-schemes
([[def-scheme]]), in which finite limits and coproducts exist
([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]],
[[cor-product-schemes-over-base-exists]]). An **augmented simplicial
$S$-scheme** is a simplicial object in this category
([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]) augmented over $S$:
$S$-schemes $X_p$ for $p\ge0$ with face maps $d_i:X_p\to X_{p-1}$ and
degeneracy maps $s_i:X_p\to X_{p+1}$ satisfying the simplicial identities,
together with structure morphisms $X_p\to S$ compatible with all of them; write
$a:X_0\to S$ for the augmentation. A **$k$-truncated** such object consists of
the data in degrees $p\le k$.

For $p\ge1$ the **matching object** $M_p(X_\bullet)$ is the finite limit
over the boundary of $[p]$: there is one copy of $X_q$ for every
order-preserving injection $\theta:[q]\hookrightarrow[p]$ with $q<p$.
For $\theta=\theta'\alpha$, compatibility is imposed by the structure map
$X(\alpha):X_r\to X_q$, where $\alpha:[q]\hookrightarrow[r]$ and
$\theta':[r]\hookrightarrow[p]$. Equivalently,
$M_p(X_\bullet)=(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$,
the value at $[p]$ of the right adjoint of the $(p-1)$-skeleton truncation;
set $M_0(X_\bullet)=S$. The **canonical boundary map** $X_p\to M_p(X_\bullet)$
is the morphism whose components are the structure maps of $X_\bullet$, and it
exists by the universal property of the limit.

A **splitting** consists of subobjects $N_q\hookrightarrow X_q$, called
the **nondegenerate parts**, such that the degeneracy maps induce isomorphisms
$$m_p:\coprod_{\delta:[p]\twoheadrightarrow[q],\ 0\le q\le p}N_q\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }X_p$$
for every $p\ge0$. The surjections are order-preserving, and the identity
surjection contributes $N_p$, not the whole $X_p$. Each component map is
$N_q\hookrightarrow X_q\xrightarrow{s_\delta}X_p$; in particular $N_0=X_0$.
The object is **split** (Deligne: *s-scinde*) if it admits such a splitting;
for a $k$-truncated object the same condition is required only for $p\le k$.
For schemes these subobjects are open-and-closed coproduct summands. Thus the
$N$-construction records nondegenerate parts, rather than adding copies of
already degenerate simplices a second time.

An augmented simplicial $S$-scheme $X_\bullet\to S$ is a **proper hypercover**
of $S$ if the augmentation $X_0\to S$ and every canonical boundary map
$X_p\to M_p(X_\bullet)$, $p\ge1$, is proper and surjective
([[def-proper-morphism]]). Neither smoothness, separatedness, finiteness nor
properness of the individual terms is part of the definition; those enter as
hypotheses where they are used.
items.strategy: Define the boundary matching limit with contravariant injection compatibility, M_0=S, and a splitting by nondegenerate N_q indexed by all ordinal surjections. The identity summand is N_p. Proper hypercovers have proper surjective matching maps. The extension and separated-target closed-limit remarks are checked in the local hyperresolution construction.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Publ. Math. IHES 44 (1974) 5-77, (6.2.1)-(6.2.4)
references.locator: (6.2.1)-(6.2.2) the N-construction and the definition of a split (scinde) simplicial object; (6.2.3)-(6.2.4) the matching-object extension data, citing SGA 4 V bis 5.1.3

items.title: Blowups of integral projective complex schemes are projective
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the Proj/Rees construction and from the eventual global generation of coherent twists; no other selection is made. The construction is otherwise explicit.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be an integral projective complex scheme of
finite type, with structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$
([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]), and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$
be a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf
([[def-quasi-coherent-ideal-sheaf]]). Then the blowup
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ of [[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]] is
projective over $\mathbb C$: for some $M\ge0$ its structure morphism factors as
a closed immersion
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$
followed by the projection. Consequently every composition of blowups of an
integral projective complex scheme along nonzero finite-type ideal sheaves
remains integral and projective over $\mathbb C$.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, an integral finite-type projective complex scheme $X$, and a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$.

[F1] [[cor-rational-map-to-projective-space-resolved-by-base-ideal-blowup]] and [[def-blowup-fractional-ideal]]: for an integral finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, an invertible sheaf $L$ and meromorphic sections $s_0,\dots,s_n$ of $L$, not all zero, with generated subsheaf $F=\sum_i\mathcal O_Xs_i\subseteq L$, the fractional blowup $B=\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_{k\ge0}(F\otimes L^{-1})^k$ is integral and $(\pi,\psi):B\to X\times_k\mathbb P^n_k$ is the schematic closure of the graph of the induced rational map, hence a closed immersion; here $F\otimes L^{-1}$ is a fractional ideal in the sense of [[def-blowup-fractional-ideal]].

[F2] [[thm-coherent-sheaves-abelian-noetherian-scheme]] and [[lem-eventual-global-generation-coherent-twists]]: on a locally Noetherian scheme a quasi-coherent module is coherent exactly when it is of finite type, so $\mathcal I$ is coherent on $X$; and on a scheme projective over the Noetherian ring $\mathbb C$ with an ample invertible sheaf $L_0$, every coherent module $G$ has $G\otimes L_0^{\otimes d}$ globally generated for all sufficiently large $d\ge d_0(G)$.

[F3] [[lem-twisting-sheaf-projective-space-ample]], [[def-very-ample-invertible-sheaf-relative]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]] and [[def-ample-invertible-sheaf]]: the twisting sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}}(1)$ is invertible with coordinate sections $x_j$ whose nonvanishing loci are exactly the standard affine charts $U_j$, and it is ample on $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$; absolute ampleness means quasi-compactness of the scheme together with an affinity test by nonvanishing loci of sections of positive powers.

[F4] [[lem-base-change-open-closed-immersions]], [[lem-closed-immersion-affine-quotient-and-base-change]] and [[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]: closed immersions are affine and Zariski-local on the target — over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ a closed immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ — they are stable under arbitrary base change, and a composite of closed immersions is again a closed immersion.

[F5] [[cor-segre-veronese-embedding]]: the bidegree-$(1,1)$ Segre map $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\to\mathbb P^{(N+1)(n+1)-1}_{\mathbb C}$ is a closed embedding.

[F6] [[lem-blowup-reduced-integral-under-domain-rees]] and [[def-integral-scheme]]: blowing up an integral scheme in a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf yields an integral scheme.

[F7] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the Axiom of Choice is the standing hypothesis, inherited here from the relative Proj construction and from the eventual global generation furnished by Serre's criterion.

1.1 $X$ carries the closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ given by its projectivity, and $L_0=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}}(1)$ is invertible. The standard charts $U_0,\dots,U_N$ are affine and cover $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$, so the finitely many intersections $X\cap U_j=X_{s_j}$, where $s_j=i^*(x_j)\in\Gamma(X,L_0)$, are affine: each is a closed subscheme of the affine chart $U_j$, hence $\operatorname{Spec}(A_j)$ for a quotient $A_j$ of the polynomial ring over $\mathbb C$ [lem-closed-immersion-affine-quotient-and-base-change]. Every $A_j$ is Noetherian [lem-field-is-noetherian, cor-finite-variable-polynomial-ring-noetherian, thm-noetherian-ring-quotients-and-localisations], so this finite affine cover exhibits the scheme $X$ as locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme, def-quasi-compact-and-quasi-separated-scheme]. The coordinate section $x_j$ has nonvanishing locus $U_j$ and pullback along a closed immersion of an invertible sheaf has as nonvanishing locus the preimage of the original one [def-very-ample-invertible-sheaf-relative, def-closed-immersion-schemes], so the charts $X_{s_j}=X\cap U_j$ are affine and cover $X$; the ampleness criterion of [def-ample-invertible-sheaf] therefore makes $L_0$ ample on $X$. [F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 By [F2] the quasi-coherent finite-type ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ is coherent on the locally Noetherian $X$, and since $X$ is projective over the Noetherian ring $\mathbb C$ and $L_0$ is ample there is $d_0$ such that $\mathcal I\otimes L_0^{\otimes d}$ is globally generated for every $d\ge d_0$. Fix $d\ge\max(1,d_0)$, put $L=L_0^{\otimes d}$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal I\otimes L\subseteq L$, and choose finitely many global sections $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ generating $\mathcal F$. To justify finiteness, global generation supplies finitely many such sections generating each finite-type stalk; their coherent cokernel vanishes on a neighbourhood of that point (on an affine chart, each of its finitely many generators is killed after localizing away from that point). Quasi-compactness of $X$ supplies finitely many of these neighbourhoods, and the union of their finite section tuples generates $\mathcal F$ everywhere. Since $\mathcal I\ne0$ and $L$ is invertible, $\mathcal F\ne0$, so not all $s_i$ are zero and $\mathcal F=\sum_i\mathcal O_Xs_i$ as subsheaves of $L$. [F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Apply [F1] to the integral finite-type $\mathbb C$-scheme $X$, the invertible sheaf $L$ and the meromorphic sections $s_0,\dots,s_n$: the fractional blowup $B=\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_{k\ge0}(\mathcal F\otimes L^{-1})^k$ is integral and $(\pi,\psi):B\to X\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ is the schematic closure of the graph of the induced rational map, hence a closed immersion. [F1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 The canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal F\otimes L^{-1}=(\mathcal I\otimes L)\otimes L^{-1}\cong\mathcal I\otimes(L\otimes L^{-1})\cong\mathcal I$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-invertible-sheaf] identify the graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\bigoplus_{k\ge0}(\mathcal F\otimes L^{-1})^k$ and $\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal I^k$, hence induce an $X$-isomorphism $B\cong\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal I^k=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ [def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal, def-blowup-fractional-ideal]. Composing with the closed immersion of step 3.1, the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ is a closed subscheme of $X\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ over $X$. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Base change of the closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ along $\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ is a closed immersion $X\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ [F4], and the Segre embedding of [F5] is a closed immersion $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$ with $M=(N+1)(n+1)-1$. A composite of closed immersions is again a closed immersion [F4], so $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$; all exhibited maps are morphisms over $\mathbb C$, so the structure morphism $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ factors as this closed immersion followed by the projection, and $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ is projective over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of [def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]. [F4, F5, step 4.1, given]

6.1 For the composition clause argue by induction on the number of factors: let $X_0$ be integral projective over $\mathbb C$ and $X_{k+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_k}X_k$ for nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaves $\mathcal I_k\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_k}$. If $X_k$ is integral projective then steps 1.1-5.1 applied to $(X_k,\mathcal I_k)$ show that $X_{k+1}$ is projective over $\mathbb C$, and [F6] shows that it stays integral, so the induction runs through every finite composition. [F6, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Boundaries and Choice accounting. An integral scheme is nonempty and $\mathcal I\ne0$ by hypothesis, so the empty and zero cases are excluded; the chosen twist satisfies $d\ge1$; the endpoint $n=0$ of a single generator is allowed, the Segre factor then being $\mathbb P^0_{\mathbb C}$ with $M=N$; and $N=0$ is covered by the same argument with the single chart $U_0$. The Axiom of Choice [F7] is inherited exactly from [F1] and [F2]; no further selection is made. [F1, F2, F7, given, cases: empty zero endpoints] ∎

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Section 31.33 (Blowing up), Lemma 31.33.13
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry (June 27, 2011 author draft), Section 19.4

items.title: Smooth projective proper hyperresolutions
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from Chow, desingularization, properness and scheme constructions and permits countably many successive smooth projective covers; every finite skeleton uses finitely many selections.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Every proper complex algebraic variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial
proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with every $Y_p$ smooth projective. Here
proper hypercover means that $Y_0\to Y$ and each map
$Y_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}Y_\bullet)_p$ is proper and surjective. Two
such systems admit a third smooth projective proper hypercover mapping to both
over $Y$. Every morphism between proper varieties can be lifted to a morphism
between such hypercovers after refining the source. Degree-$n$ cohomology uses
only the finite skeleton through degree $n+1$.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and a proper complex algebraic variety $Y$, i.e. a separated finite-type $\mathbb C$-scheme $Y$ whose structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ is universally closed ([[def-proper-morphism]]).

[F1] [[thm-weak-embedded-desingularization]] and [[lem-blowups-of-projective-schemes-are-projective]]: for a smooth finite-type $\mathbb C$-scheme $X$ and a reduced closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$, the embedded desingularization is a tower of blowups of $X$ along regular centers whose strict transform $\widetilde Z$ is smooth, maps to $Z$ properly and birationally on every irreducible component, and is an isomorphism over the smooth locus; each stage of the tower is a blowup of an integral projective scheme along a finite-type ideal sheaf (the empty center giving the identity), so if $X=\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ the strict transform $\widetilde Z$ is smooth projective and $\widetilde Z\to Z$ is proper and surjective.

[F2] [[lem-chow-lemma-proper-noetherian]]: for a Noetherian base $S$ and a separated finite-type $S$-scheme $T$ there are a scheme $T'$ and morphisms $\pi:T'\to T$ proper surjective and $\iota:T'\to\mathbb P^N_S$ an immersion over $S$; if $T\to S$ is proper then $\iota$ is a closed immersion, so $T'$ is projective over $S$.

[F3] [[def-split-augmented-simplicial-objects-and-matching-objects]], [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]] and [[cor-product-schemes-over-base-exists]]: the matching object $M_p$ is the finite limit of the boundary diagram over the augmentation base. A splitting is a collection of nondegenerate summands $N_q\subseteq Y_q$ with $Y_p=\coprod_{[p]\twoheadrightarrow[q]}N_q$. The structure maps are contravariant ordinal maps, and every ordinal map factors uniquely as a surjection followed by an injection.

[F4] [[lem-proper-stable-base-change]], [[lem-proper-stable-composition]], [[lem-proper-source-to-separated-target-proper]], [[lem-closed-immersion-proper]] and [[thm-projective-morphism-proper]]: proper morphisms are stable under base change and composition; closed immersions and projective morphisms are proper; a morphism from a proper complex scheme to a separated complex scheme is proper. Surjectivity is stable under base change by [[lem-base-change-surjective-morphisms]] and under composition directly.

[F5] [[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]], [[cor-segre-veronese-embedding]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]], [[def-separated-morphism-schemes]] and [[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]: finite products of projective complex schemes are projective by the Segre embedding. Finite limits with separated targets are closed in those products, since each equality of two maps is the inverse image of a closed diagonal. Finite disjoint unions are also projective: embed the components in mutually disjoint coordinate linear subspaces of one projective space, and take their closed union. These subspaces have no common geometric point, so the union is the scheme coproduct.

[F6] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the Axiom of Choice is the standing hypothesis, inherited here from Chow's lemma, from the embedded desingularization and from the countably many selections of smooth projective covers in the induction (finitely many for each truncation).

1.1 Smooth projective covers. Let $Z$ be a reduced projective complex scheme with its closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$. The ambient scheme $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ is smooth of finite type over the characteristic-zero field $\mathbb C$, so [F1] applies to the reduced closed subscheme $Z$: the embedded desingularization is a tower $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}=X_0\leftarrow X_1\leftarrow\dots\leftarrow X_r$ of blowups along regular centers with strict transform $\widetilde Z=Z_r$ smooth, mapping to $Z$ properly and birationally on every irreducible component and isomorphically over the smooth locus. Each $X_i$ is integral projective over $\mathbb C$ by [[lem-blowups-of-projective-schemes-are-projective]], so the closed subscheme $\widetilde Z\subseteq X_r$ is smooth projective, and $\widetilde Z\to Z$ is surjective because its image is closed and contains a dense open of every irreducible component of the reduced $Z$. [F1, given, construct]

2.1 Degree zero. Apply [F2] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ Noetherian and $T=Y$ proper, hence separated and of finite type: there are a projective $X'$ over $\mathbb C$ and a proper surjective $\pi:X'\to Y$. Replacing $X'$ by its reduction ([[def-reduction-of-scheme]]) is a closed immersion $X'_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X'$ that is proper and surjective onto $X'$, and the reduced projective $Z=X'_{\mathrm{red}}$ still maps properly and surjectively to $Y$; step 1.1 applied to $Z$ produces a smooth projective $Y_0$ with a proper surjective $Y_0\to Y$. This is the degree-zero term of the construction, and the one-term object $\{Y_0\to Y\}$ is a split $0$-truncated proper hypercover in the sense of [F3], its only boundary map being the augmentation. [F2, F3, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Matching objects are projective. Suppose a split $(p-1)$-truncated proper hypercover $Y_0,\dots,Y_{p-1}$ of $Y$ with all terms smooth projective has been constructed, for some $p\ge1$. Let $B_p$ be the finite set of order-preserving injections $\theta:[q]\hookrightarrow[p]$ with $q<p$, and write $q(\theta)=q$. The matching object $M_p$ is cut out in $\prod_{\theta\in B_p,Y}Y_{q(\theta)}$ by the boundary compatibility equations. Each equation is an equality into a separated lower term, so [F5] makes it closed. This fibre product is closed in $\prod_{\theta\in B_p,\mathbb C}Y_{q(\theta)}$ by the closed diagonal of $Y$. The factors are projective over $\mathbb C$; their finite product and its closed subscheme $M_p$ are projective by [F5]. Hence $M_p$ is projective over $\mathbb C$. [F3, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Extension step. Choose a smooth projective proper surjection $N_p\to M_p$ by applying step 1.1 to the reduction of the projective $M_p$; the reduction inclusion is proper surjective by [F4]. Set $Y_p=\coprod_{\delta:[p]\twoheadrightarrow[q],\,q\le p}N_q$, using the previously chosen $N_q$ for $q<p$. Here is the explicit extension of the structure maps. Write $i_q:N_q\to Y_q$ for the summand inclusions. For any $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ with $m,n\le p$, on the summand $N_q$ of $Y_n$ indexed by $\delta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[q]$, factor $\delta\alpha=\iota\epsilon$ with $\epsilon:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[t]$ and $\iota:[t]\hookrightarrow[q]$. Its map into $Y_m$ is $Y(\epsilon)Y(\iota)i_q$. The injection part is an old structure map if $q<p$, a component of the chosen boundary tuple if $q=p$ and $t<p$, and the identity if $t=q=p$. The surjection part, when $m=p$ and $t<p$, sends each old summand $N_u$ indexed by $\eta:[t]\twoheadrightarrow[u]$ into the new summand indexed by $\eta\epsilon$; otherwise it is old or the identity. Boundary compatibility supplies the relations between injections; concatenation supplies the relations between surjections; refactoring their composites gives the mixed relations. Thus these prescriptions obey contravariant composition and define the $p$-truncated simplicial object. Its splitting is precisely the displayed coproduct. Each summand is smooth projective, and each map to the separated projective $M_p$ is proper by [F4]. The finite union map is proper (finite type and separatedness hold on its open-and-closed summands, and every base change has closed image as a finite union of closed images); it is surjective on the $N_p$ summand. This extends the proper hypercover through degree $p$. [F3, F4, F5, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Existence and finite stages. AC permits successive choices in step 4.1 for all $p$, giving one compatible augmented simplicial object; each term is smooth projective and each matching map proper surjective. In a first-quadrant cochain simple complex $K^{p,q}$ attached to this object, total degrees $n-1,n,n+1$ involve only $p\le n+1$. Thus its degree-$n$ cohomology uses only this finite skeleton. No splitness of the higher terms of $\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NY_\bullet$ is asserted or needed. [F3, F6, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Relative refinement construction. More generally let $T_\bullet\to Y$ be a proper hypercover with projective complex terms, without a smoothness or splitting assumption. Construct a split smooth projective $V_\bullet\to Y$ with a map to $T_\bullet$. At degree zero take a smooth projective proper cover of $T_0$. Once the lower degrees and their maps are constructed, form $P_p=T_p\times_{M_p(T)}M_p(V)$. This is projective by [F5], and $P_p\to M_p(V)$ is a proper surjection by base change of the matching map of $T$. Choose a smooth projective proper cover $N_p\to P_p$, and apply step 4.1 to its composite into $M_p(V)$. On $N_p$ define the map into $T_p$ by the other projection; on each degenerate summand $N_q$ define it by its existing map to $T_q$ followed by the corresponding degeneracy of $T$. The fibre-product condition and the composition check of step 4.1 give a simplicial map. Its new matching map is proper surjective on $N_p$, so the induction constructs the required $V$. This uses no inference that termwise surjections induce surjections on matching limits. [F3, F4, F5, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct]

7.1 Common refinements and morphisms. For two given hypercovers $A_\bullet,B_\bullet$ of $Y$, put $T_p=A_p\times_YB_p$. Matching limits commute with these products, so the matching map of $T$ is the product over $Y$ of the matching maps of $A,B$; it is proper surjective by [F4]. Its terms are projective by [F5]. Step 6.1 gives a split smooth projective hypercover mapping to $T$ and hence to both given systems. For a morphism $g:Y\to Z$, and fixed hypercovers $A_\bullet\to Y$ and $B_\bullet\to Z$, instead put $T_p=A_p\times_ZB_p$, using $A_p\to Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$. This is the product over $Y$ of $A$ with the base-changed hypercover $Y\times_ZB$, so its matching maps are again proper surjective; its terms are closed in $A_p\times_{\mathbb C}B_p$ by separatedness of $Z$, hence projective. Apply step 6.1 over $Y$. The resulting maps to $A$ and $B$ give the required refinement of the source and lift of $g$. [F3, F4, F5, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 Boundaries and Choice accounting. For empty $Y$ take every term empty; degree zero is step 2.1. If $Y$ is a point, the constant one-point hypercover is allowed (its $N_p$ are empty for $p>0$). Zero-dimensional and mixed-dimensional smooth terms are finite disjoint unions covered by [F5]. AC is inherited from Chow's lemma and desingularization and permits the countable sequence of cover choices, including the relative constructions; any fixed finite truncation uses only finitely many such choices. [F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, step 5.1, step 7.1, cases: empty zero one degenerate endpoints] ∎

items.title: Borel-Moore homology by locally finite chains
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition or in the induced proper pushforward.
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological space and let $R$ be a
commutative ring. For $k\ge0$ let $S_k(X)$ be the set of continuous maps
$\Delta^k\to X$ from the standard simplex
([[def-singular-simplex-and-singular-chain-group-with-coefficients]]); the
convention of [[lem-a-locally-compact-hausdorff-space-has-a-base-of-open-sets-with-compact-closure]]
supplies neighbourhood bases by open sets with compact closure. A formal sum
$c=\sum_{\sigma\in S_k(X)}a_\sigma\,\sigma$ with $a_\sigma\in R$ is **locally
finite** if every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood meeting only
finitely many of the images $\sigma(\Delta^k)$ of the simplices with
$a_\sigma\ne0$ ([[def-compact-space]] for compactness). The **locally finite
$k$-chains** are the $R$-module
$$C_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)=\bigl\{c:\ \text{the sum is locally finite}\bigr\},\qquad C_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)=0\ \ (k<0),$$
with addition and scalar multiplication defined coefficientwise. The **boundary**
$$\partial\Bigl(\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma\Bigr)=\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\,\partial\sigma$$
is again locally finite, because every face of $\sigma$ has image contained in
the image of $\sigma$, and $\partial^2=0$ because $\partial^2\sigma=0$; thus
$(C_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R),\partial)$ is a chain complex and its homology is the
**Borel-Moore homology** $H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)$
([[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]] for the ordinary chain
complex, which is the special case of sums with finite support).

A **proper** continuous map $f:X\to Y$ (inverse images of compact sets are
compact) induces $f_*:C_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\to C_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y;R)$ by
$\sigma\mapsto f\circ\sigma$: for $y\in Y$ choose a compact neighbourhood $K$
of $y$; the compact set $f^{-1}(K)$ is covered by finitely many of the
neighbourhoods furnished by local finiteness of $c$, so only finitely many
simplices meet $f^{-1}(K)$, and a neighbourhood of $y$ contained in $K$ then
meets only finitely many images $f(\sigma(\Delta^k))$. This is a chain map
because $f\circ\partial\sigma=\partial(f\circ\sigma)$, so it induces
$f_*:H_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\to H_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y;R)$. Coefficients and degree
are otherwise unused below. No choice principle is used in the definition; a
homeomorphism and, more generally, a proper continuous map act functorially.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. The clauses fix local finiteness, the boundary complex, the containment of ordinary chains and the proper-pushforward functoriality used by the companion theorem; the agreement with ordinary homology for compact spaces is proved separately on this page.

items.title: Borel-Moore and ordinary homology agree for compact spaces
items.axiom_use: The proof is choice-free: local finiteness supplies an open cover by small neighbourhoods and compactness extracts a finite subcover, with no selection of points or simplices.
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff topological space and let $R$ be a commutative
ring. The inclusion of the ordinary singular chain complex into the complex of
locally finite chains of [[def-borel-moore-homology]] is an isomorphism of chain
complexes, and it induces isomorphisms
$$H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H_k^{\mathrm{sing}}(X;R)$$
in every degree, natural for continuous maps of compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]]). In particular the class
map of a proper complex algebraic variety may be computed using ordinary
singular homology.
items.strategy:
**Given:** A compact Hausdorff space $X$, a commutative ring $R$, and the locally finite chain complex of [[def-borel-moore-homology]].

[F1] [[def-borel-moore-homology]]: $C_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)$ consists of formal sums $\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma$ over continuous $k$-simplices such that every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood meeting only finitely many images of the simplices with nonzero coefficient; the boundary is coefficientwise; ordinary singular chains are the sums with finite support, and a proper continuous map induces a pushforward on locally finite chains.

[F2] [[def-compact-space]] and [[def-continuous-map-top]]: a space is compact when every open cover has a finite subcover, and continuity makes preimages of open sets open. By [[thm-compact-subset-of-a-hausdorff-space-is-closed]] a compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed, and by [[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]] a closed subspace of a compact space is compact.

1.1 Every ordinary singular chain is locally finite: a sum with finite support has only finitely many distinct images, so any neighbourhood of any point meets at most those finitely many images. The inclusion $C_k(X;R)\hookrightarrow C_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)$ is therefore defined, commutes with the coefficientwise boundary, and is injective. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Conversely let $c=\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma$ be locally finite on the compact $X$. Local finiteness provides an open cover of $X$ by neighbourhoods $U$ each of which meets only finitely many images of simplices with nonzero coefficient; by compactness [F2] finitely many such neighbourhoods $U_1,\dots,U_m$ cover $X$. If $\sigma$ has $a_\sigma\ne0$, then its image is nonempty, so it meets some $U_j$, and for each $j$ only finitely many such $\sigma$ meet $U_j$; hence only finitely many coefficients are nonzero and $c$ lies in the image of the inclusion. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 By steps 1.1 and 1.2 the inclusion is a bijection on every chain group, hence an isomorphism of chain complexes; it induces isomorphisms on homology. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of compact Hausdorff spaces, for every compact $K\subseteq Y$, Hausdorffness makes $K$ closed, continuity makes $f^{-1}(K)$ closed in the compact $X$, and this preimage is therefore compact by [F2]. Thus $f$ is proper, and the pushforward $f_*$ of [F1] restricts on finite chains to the ordinary singular chain map, so the isomorphisms are natural. No choice principle was used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Proper cohomology and functorial mixed Hodge weights
items.axiom_use: AC inherited from hyperresolutions, descent, Godement exact products and comparison complements, singular/sheaf comparison, partition of unity (including its DC hypothesis), and extending independent sets to bases for finite-dimensional homology duality.
items.statement:
Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex
algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) with weights at most $n$. For a
morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback
$H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on
$U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of pure dimension $d$, the
proper homological class map
$$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$
is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and
consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure.
No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed. For an ambient $X$ with components of
different dimensions, the class map is the direct sum of these maps on
$Y\times_X X_c\to X_c$, using each component dimension $d_c$ separately.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and a proper complex algebraic variety $Y$; morphisms $g:Y\to U$ to a smooth quasiprojective $U$ and $h:Y\to X$ to a smooth projective $X$ of pure dimension $d$ where these are named.

[F1] [[thm-proper-varieties-admit-smooth-projective-hyperresolutions]]: every proper complex variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with all $Y_p$ smooth projective; two such hypercovers are dominated by a third smooth projective one; every morphism of proper varieties lifts to a morphism of such hypercovers after refining the source; and degree-$n$ cohomology uses only the skeleton through degree $n+1$.

[F2] [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]]: for a proper hypercover $X_\bullet\to X$ of finite-type complex varieties and a bounded-below constructible coefficient complex $F$ of lower bound $a$, the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism $F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_pRa_{p*}a_p^*F$, giving $R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F)$ and a strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$ whose diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite and determined by levels $p\le m-a+1$, and all refinements induce the same comparison. For the constant rational complex $F=\mathbb Q_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the spectral sequence is first-quadrant.

[F3] [[lem-mixed-hodge-complexes-give-functorial-cohomology-and-simplicial-weights]] and [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]: part (ii) turns a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative bidegrees, with strict differentials and pure cohomology of weight $q$ in bidegree $(p,q)$, into a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex whose simple complex carries a mixed Hodge structure with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, so that all weights of $H^n$ are at most $n$ when only nonnegative cosimplicial degrees occur.

[F4] [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] and [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]: a smooth projective complex scheme $Z$ of pure dimension has analytification $Z^{\mathrm{an}}$ a compact Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold carrying a Kähler form from any ample class, and $H^q(Z,\mathbb Q)$ is pure of weight $q$ with functorial rational structure and strict Hodge filtration; for a finite disjoint union of such schemes the statements hold componentwise and sum.

[F5] [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]: mixed Hodge morphisms are strict for both filtrations, their kernels, images and cokernels carry mixed Hodge structures, and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ to a structure of weights at most $n$ has pure image of weight $n$.

[F6] [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]], [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-open-stars-have-explicit-conical-product-charts]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]], [[thm-a-compact-hausdorff-space-is-regular-and-normal]], [[cor-compact-hausdorff-partitions-of-unity]] and [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]: the analytic topology of a complex algebraic variety is fixed by the cited definition; the triangulation theorem provides finite compatible smooth Whitney refinements and triangulations of quasi-projective charts; open stars of simplices have explicit conical product charts and are contractible; a compact Hausdorff space is normal, has subordinate continuous partitions of unity under AC and its DC consequence; and the metric comparison identifies derived constant-sheaf cohomology with singular cohomology on every open subset once the metric and contractible-open basis are constructed in step 2.1.

[F7] [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]: for smooth quasiprojective $U$ with an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the logarithmic de Rham complex with its pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ of weights at least $n$, independent of the compactification, with $W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U,\mathbb Q))$. Its empty-boundary construction gives the exact functorial Godement global-section model of the holomorphic de Rham complex of a smooth projective variety, with the degree Hodge filtration and the constant-sheaf rational comparison; the proof derives differential strictness from Hodge-de Rham $E_1$ degeneration.

[F8] [[thm-every-independent-set-extends-to-a-basis]], [[def-borel-moore-homology]], [[lem-borel-moore-homology-of-compact-spaces]], [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]] and [[prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula]]: under AC an independent set extends to a basis; locally finite chains define Borel-Moore homology, which agrees with ordinary singular homology for compact spaces; for compact spaces and field coefficients cohomology is dual to homology via the Kronecker pairing; and on a compact oriented $2d$-manifold cap product with the fundamental class is an isomorphism $H^{2d-i}\to H_i$ compatible with the cup product and the trace.

[F9] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the standing hypothesis, inherited from the hyperresolution, descent and logarithmic suppliers, including the AC used in the exact Godement resolutions of [F7] and in the sheaf-singular comparison of [F6]. AC also supplies the partition of unity in step 2.1 (and implies its DC hypothesis).

1.1 (Actual cosimplicial Hodge complexes.) Choose the smooth projective proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ of [F1]. Use the exact functorial Godement construction of [F7], applied on every $Y_p$, and put $K_{\mathbb Q}^{p,q}=\Gamma(Y_p,C^q(\mathbb Q_{Y_p}))$ and $K_{\mathbb C}^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{k+t=q}\Gamma(Y_p,C^t(\Omega^k_{Y_p}))$, for $p,q\ge0$, with $F^b$ given by $k\ge b$. These are the resolved global de Rham complexes, not the complex of global holomorphic forms. Godement pullback along each face is induced by pulling a germ collection at a point to the stalk over its image; the successive cokernels preserve these maps, so their composites obey the simplicial identities and preserve $F$. The constant inclusion $\mathbb Q\otimes\mathbb C\to\Omega^0$ gives the functorial rational comparison; on cohomology it is the scalar-extension comparison of [F4]. Exactness and acyclicity of the resolution show $H^q(K_{\mathbb C}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb C)$, with the holomorphic-degree image filtration, and $H^q(K_{\mathbb Q}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$. The compact Hodge theorem [F4] gives pure weight $q$ and Hodge-de Rham $E_1$ degeneration on each smooth projective component. The latter makes the actual internal differential $F$-strict: if $dx\in F^b$, degeneration lifts the leading lower-filtration class of $x$ to a cycle up to a higher-filtration term and a boundary; subtracting the cycle and boundary raises the preimage filtration without changing $dx$, and finite induction supplies a preimage in $F^b$, as in the strict correction of [F7]. Thus every level is an actual weight-zero rational Hodge complex. Each internal total diagonal is finite, and $F^{q+1}K^{p,q}=0$, so [F3] applies to its first-quadrant simple complex, giving the mixed Hodge structure and $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$, $E_2$ degeneration and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=E_2^{n-q,q}$. The terms have $p=n-q\ge0$, so weights are at most $n$, and the finitely many $E_1^{p,q}$ entries on every total diagonal are finite-dimensional by [F4]. Descent [F2] identifies the rational simple cohomology naturally with $H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$, carrying this structure. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

2.1 Singular comparison. The point map $Y_0^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a continuous surjection: a nonempty finite-type fibre over a complex point has a complex closed point, as in the residue-field argument of [F4]'s analytification supplier. Thus $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact. A finite affine cover makes it second-countable, and separatedness makes its diagonal closed in the products of these affine point loci; hence it is Hausdorff. The topology of a nonreduced scheme is that of its reduction. On each affine chart [F6] supplies a finite deleted-boundary triangulation. At a point of a retained simplex, its open star is $\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(L)$. Small convex neighbourhoods of the point in the first factor and small radial cones in the second give a contractible open neighbourhood basis: compactness of the link gives a uniform radial bound at the apex. To obtain a metric, take a finite partition of unity $\phi_j$ subordinate to the affine charts, with supports contained in the charts, using [F6]. If $z_j$ are the finite affine coordinate vectors, define $\Phi(y)=(\phi_j(y),\phi_j(y)z_j(y))_j$, extending each product by zero outside its chart. These extensions are continuous because the supports are closed and contained in their charts. If $\Phi(y)=\Phi(y')$, choose $j$ with $\phi_j(y)>0$; equality of the scalar coordinates puts both points in that chart with equal positive $\phi_j$, and equality of the product coordinates gives $z_j(y)=z_j(y')$, hence $y=y'$. A continuous injection from this compact space to Hausdorff Euclidean space is a homeomorphism onto its image: images of closed subsets are compact and therefore closed. Pulling back the Euclidean metric gives the analytic topology. The sheaf-singular comparison of [F6] now identifies the descended cohomology with $H^n_{\mathrm{sing}}(Y^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Q)$, naturally in $Y$. The partition and comparison consume their stated AC hypotheses; no claim of a DC-only construction is made. [F4, F6, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Independence and functoriality. If $a':Y'_\bullet\to Y$ is a second split proper hypercover with smooth projective terms, [F1] supplies a third such hypercover dominating both; the two refinements give filtered comparison maps between the corresponding cosimplicial systems and hence morphisms of the mixed Hodge complexes of step 1.1, and by [F2] both simple complexes compute the constant-sheaf cohomology of $Y$, so the induced maps on $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ are the identity; strictness [F5] upgrades this to an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures, so the structure is independent of the diagram. A morphism $g:Y\to Y'$ of proper varieties lifts, after refining the source hypercover, to a morphism of the chosen hypercovers [F1], pullback of holomorphic forms along it is a morphism of the cosimplicial mixed Hodge complexes compatible with the comparisons, and independence of the hypercovers makes the induced map $g^*:H^n(Y',\mathbb Q)\to H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ well defined and compatible with identities and composition. [F1, F2, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

3.2 (The smooth-open clause and the actual total map.) Let $g:Y\to U$ and choose the logarithmic comparison model on $X\supset U$ from [F7]. Define its pullback into the simple complex of step 1.1 to be supported in cosimplicial degree zero, using $g_0=ga_0:Y_0\to U$. Pullback of a logarithmic form is regular on $Y_0$: a boundary equation pulls back to a nowhere-zero holomorphic function, whose $d\log$ is regular. Apply the functorial Godement resolutions to obtain the internal chain map into $K_{\mathbb C}^{0,*}$ preserving holomorphic degree. Its first alternating face differential is zero, since $g_0d_0=g_0d_1$ on $Y_1$, so this degree-zero-supported map is an actual chain map into the simple total complex; no map into every positive cosimplicial degree is being implicitly summed. On the rational side the natural pullback from $Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$ along $jg_0$, with the augmentation comparison, gives the same degree-zero-supported map, and it is compatible with the logarithmic meridian comparison up to the permitted filtered homotopies. For weight indices $a<0$ the source pole filtration is zero; for $a\ge0$ the target $L_a$ is the whole first-quadrant simple complex, so the map preserves weights. It preserves $F$ by form degree. Thus it is a morphism of the mixed Hodge complexes, and descent identifies its cohomology map with the actual rational pullback $g^*:H^n(U;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$. The functoriality clause of [F3] makes this a mixed Hodge morphism. [F2, F3, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 The class map. Let $h:Y\to X$ be proper with $X$ smooth projective of pure dimension $d$. By step 2.1 and [F8], Borel-Moore homology of $Y$ equals ordinary homology. The Kronecker isomorphism $H^i(Y)=H_i(Y)^*$ and finite-dimensionality of $H^i(Y)$ imply that $H_i(Y)$ is finite-dimensional: any finite independent tuple extends to a basis by [F8] under AC and gives that many independent coordinate functionals, so its length is bounded by $\dim H^i(Y)$. Consequently evaluation identifies $H_i(Y)=H^i(Y)^*$ canonically. Give it the dual filtrations of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. Their weight-$a$ graded piece is $(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-a}H^i(Y))^*$, with pure types $(p,q)$ changed to $(-p,-q)$; this proves the mixed Hodge axiom and the lower weight bound $-i$. Transposes of filtration-preserving maps preserve the annihilator filtrations. Naturality of the Kronecker pairing identifies $h_*$ with the transpose of $h^*$, a mixed Hodge morphism by step 3.1. For $X$, cup product preserves Hodge type by [F4], and the top cohomology on each connected component is of type $(d,d)$: forms with total degree $2d$ have only that possible type. Evaluation on the oriented fundamental classes therefore gives a Hodge morphism $H^{2d}(X)\to\mathbb Q(-d)$ (sum the component traces). Poincare duality and the cap/cup identity [F8] make the resulting cup/trace pairing $H^i(X)\otimes H^{2d-i}(X)\to\mathbb Q(-d)$ perfect. After twisting the second factor by $(d)$ it identifies $H^{2d-i}(X)(d)$ with $H^i(X)^*=H_i(X)$ as pure Hodge structures of weight $-i$: the complementary types become $(-p,-q)$ on the dual factor. The composite with $h_*$ is the asserted class map. By [F5] its image is pure of weight $-i$; untwisting gives weight $2d-i$. For mixed-dimensional $X$, apply this on its finitely many open-and-closed connected components and the corresponding inverse images in $Y$, obtaining the stated direct sum. [F4, F5, F8, F9, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Boundaries and Choice accounting. For $Y=\varnothing$ every group is zero with the trivial structure and all clauses are vacuous; the degree $n=0$ case has all weights equal to $0$, consistent with the bound; the smooth hypercover terms of differing dimensions are handled componentwise in [F4], without assuming that the singular components of $Y$ are disjoint; and the case $Y=X$ of pure dimension $d$ reduces the class map to Poincare duality itself. The Axiom of Choice [F9] is inherited from [F1], [F2] and [F7], including the exact resolutions, comparison data and sheaf-singular comparison; it also licenses the partition in step 2.1 and the duality argument in step 4.1. [F1, F2, F6, F7, F9, given, cases: empty zero one degenerate endpoints] ∎

items.title: Weights control restriction images into proper varieties
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the logarithmic Hodge and proper-weight suppliers only; the strictness computation itself makes no selection.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any smooth projective compactification, and let
$g:Y\to U$ be a morphism with $Y$ proper (possibly singular and reducible).
Then, in every degree $n$,
$$\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{(jg)^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q))=\operatorname{im}(H^n(U,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{g^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)).$$
Both images are pure Hodge substructures of weight $n$. This includes the
restriction of a smooth projective total space to a proper singular fiber through
an open subvariety, which is the exact use in de Cataldo-Migliorini
Proposition 8.3.2 of arXiv:math/0306030v1 (pp. 64-65).
items.strategy:
**Given:** AC, a smooth quasiprojective $U$ with a smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and a morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper.

[F1] [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]: the logarithmic mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ has weights at least $n$ and satisfies $W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(j^*:H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U,\mathbb Q))$ for every smooth projective compactification, independently of the chosen $j$; for a non-SNC boundary the logarithmic theorem proves the same actual image formula by SNC domination and its modification-image supplier.

[F2] [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]]: the proper variety $Y$ carries a functorial mixed Hodge structure on each $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ with $W_nH^n(Y,\mathbb Q)=H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, and the pullback $g^*:H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ for the actual morphism $g:Y\to U$ with proper $Y$ and smooth quasiprojective $U$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on the source.

[F3] [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]] and [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]: a mixed Hodge morphism $f$ is $W$-strict, so $f(W_a)=f(H)\cap W_aK$ for every $a$; its image with the induced filtration is a mixed Hodge structure; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ to a structure of weights at most $n$ has pure image of weight $n$.

[F4] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the standing hypothesis, inherited from the two cited theorems.

1.1 By [F3] applied to the mixed Hodge morphism $g^*$ and the strictness identity $g^*(W_nH^n(U))=\operatorname{im}g^*\cap W_nH^n(Y)$, the target weight bound $W_nH^n(Y)=H^n(Y)$ of [F2] reduces the right-hand side to $\operatorname{im}g^*$; by [F1] the image of $W_nH^n(U)$ under $g^*$ is $g^*(\operatorname{im}j^*)=\operatorname{im}(g^*j^*)=\operatorname{im}((jg)^*)$. Hence the two asserted images agree as actual subspaces of $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, without choosing a splitting of the weight filtration on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Put $I=\operatorname{im}g^*$. Strictness gives $W_{n-1}I=g^*(W_{n-1}H^n(U))$, and by [F1] the source has weights at least $n$, so $W_{n-1}I=0$; the target bound gives $W_nI=I$. Hence the induced mixed Hodge structure on $I$ is pure of weight $n$, and by step 1.1 the image of $(jg)^*$ is the same pure substructure. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Boundaries and Choice accounting. If $U=\varnothing$ or $Y=\varnothing$ all groups vanish and the claim is vacuous; the degree $n=0$ case gives weight-zero images by the same strictness argument; the case $U=X$ has $j=\mathrm{id}$ and $W_nH^n(U)=H^n(U)$, so both images are the full image of $g^*$, consistent with the statement; and $Y$ smooth or reduced is not required, the target bound being the only hypothesis on the target. The Axiom of Choice [F4] is inherited from [F1] and [F2]; no selection is made in this argument. [F1, F2, F4, given, cases: empty zero one degenerate endpoints] ∎

items.title: A proper singular curve with weight-zero cohomology
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through normalization, projective properness, cohomological descent, proper weights and the field-dual homology comparison. All displayed tuple and differential computations are finite and make no further selections.
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $C$ be an integral complex projective
curve whose normalization $\nu:\mathbb P^1\to C$ is an isomorphism outside a
single ordinary node, with two distinct points above that node. Then
$H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ is one-dimensional of weight $0$, illustrating that proper
singular cohomology need not be pure of its degree.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), an integral complex rational projective curve $C$ with a single singular point, an ordinary node, and its normalization $\nu:\mathbb P^1\to C$ identifying two distinct points $a,b$ and an isomorphism over the complement of the node.

[F1] [[cor-normalization-resolves-singularities-of-curves]] and [[cor-finite-morphism-proper]]: the normalization of an integral projective curve over a perfect field is a nonsingular projective curve and the normalization map is finite and birational, hence proper and surjective; for the rational nodal curve the normalization is $\mathbb P^1$ and $\nu$ is an isomorphism over the smooth locus.

[F2] [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]] and [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]]: the Cech nerve of a proper surjection is a proper hypercover, its descent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C_p,\mathbb Q)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(C,\mathbb Q)$ is strongly convergent with finite diagonals, and for a proper hypercover with smooth projective terms the associated mixed Hodge complex has $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(C,\mathbb Q)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$ with weights at most $n$.

[F4] [[def-reduction-of-scheme]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]] and [[lem-proper-source-to-separated-target-proper]]: reduction keeps the underlying points and kills nilpotents; fibre products represent compatible tuples; projective complex schemes are proper by [[thm-projective-morphism-proper]], and a morphism from a proper complex scheme to a separated complex scheme is proper. The matching and split conventions are those of [[def-split-augmented-simplicial-objects-and-matching-objects]].

[F3] [[thm-stereographic-projection-riemann-sphere-homeomorphism]], [[cor-homology-of-spheres]] and [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]: $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\cong S^2$, so $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ and $H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$, the latter as the dual of $H_1(S^2;\mathbb Q)=0$; also $H^2(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ and all higher groups vanish.

1.1 Use the reduced Cech nerve $C_p=(\mathbb P^1\times_C\cdots\times_C\mathbb P^1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, with $p+1$ factors and maps deleting or repeating entries. Reduction is functorial: a map from a reduced scheme kills nilpotents and hence factors through the target reduction. The underlying points off the node form the diagonal; over the node the tuples are in $\{a,b\}^{p+1}$. The diagonal is a closed immersion, and its complement consists of the $2^{p+1}-2$ mixed tuples, an open finite set of closed complex points. This set is also closed, so these points and the diagonal are open-and-closed components. The mixed components are reduced points. The reduced diagonal component equals $\mathbb P^1$: its closed immersion has the whole underlying support, so its ideal lies in the zero nilradical of that reduced component. Thus $C_p=\mathbb P^1_d\sqcup T_p$ is smooth projective. Every compatible boundary tuple of geometric points has exactly the $p+1$ compatible vertices of the Cech nerve, so it lifts to $C_p$; this proves surjectivity of every matching map, even if its target has nilpotents. These maps are proper by [F4], since their sources are projective and the finite matching limits are separated. The augmentation is proper surjective by [F1]. The reduced nerve is also split: repeated adjacent entries are degeneracies, and compressing successive equal entries gives the unique alternating nondegenerate tuple; for $p=0$ the nondegenerate part is $\mathbb P^1$. Apply [F2]. Its row $E_1^{p,0}$ has one copy of $\mathbb Q$ for the diagonal and one per mixed tuple; by [F3] the positive rows vanish except for the single diagonal copy in degree two. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Compute the degree-zero row in low degrees. On $C_0=\mathbb P^1$ one has $E_1^{0,0}=\mathbb Q$, and on $C_1=\mathbb P^1_d\sqcup\{ab\}\sqcup\{ba\}$ one has $E_1^{1,0}=\mathbb Q_d\oplus\mathbb Q_{ab}\oplus\mathbb Q_{ba}$; the alternating sum of the two face pullbacks $\delta^0$ sends a constant to the differences of the two diagonal values, hence is zero. On $C_2$ the six nonconstant tuples contribute the coordinates for $(aab),(aba),(abb),(baa),(bab),(bba)$, and evaluating the alternating sum $\delta^1(c)$ on these components and on the diagonal gives $c_d$ on the diagonal and on $(aab),(abb),(baa),(bba)$, and $c_{ab}+c_{ba}-c_d$ on $(aba),(bab)$, where $c=(c_d,c_{ab},c_{ba})$. Hence $\delta^1(c)=0$ exactly when $c_d=0$ and $c_{ba}=-c_{ab}$, so $E_2^{1,0}=\ker\delta^1/\operatorname{im}\delta^0$ is one-dimensional, generated by $(0,1,-1)$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The other total-degree-one entry is $E_1^{0,1}=H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$ by [F3], so it contributes nothing; the spectral sequence is first-quadrant with finite diagonals and degenerates at $E_2$ by [F2]. Therefore $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)\cong E_2^{1,0}$ is one-dimensional, and by the weight identification of [F2] its graded pieces are $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0H^1=E_2^{1,0}=\mathbb Q$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_1H^1=E_2^{0,1}=0$. The first-quadrant weight identification also makes all graded pieces of negative weight zero; together with the upper bound $1$ and finiteness of the weight filtration, this gives $W_{-1}H^1=0$ and $W_0H^1=H^1$: the whole one-dimensional space is pure of weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), as asserted. [F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
